_comment_ram_governor: 0.6 = measured 2026-08-27 (fleet-ops#1168: 10 live workers, subtrees ~470MB total, 11.5GB MemAvailable under load, p95 per-worker <0.5GB) + margin; hard backstops exist (user-1000.slice MemoryHigh=12G, oomd 80%). The governor is sized on the TYPICAL worker, not the worst case. Admission keeps cgroup memory.current (honest cgroup cost); process VmRSS is not what the cgroup charges. The 2026-08-26 sample (fleet-ops#202) had memory.current p95=822.6 MB (p95_bytes=862556160) and process VmRSS p95=35 MB; the 2026-08-27 rolling sample is memory.current p95=1163.1 MB and process VmRSS p95=2.8 MB. /proc/pressure/memory some avg10 was 1.53. fleet-ops#489 kept memory.current as the metric and briefly set ram_gb_per_worker = min(memory.current p95 * 3, 1.5) = 1.5; fleet-ops#1168 replaced that clamp with this measured 0.6 budget. Re-measure both with bin/ram-metric-compare (heartbeat section 14). The 1.28 that was here before 2026-08-26 was the median of completed-unit MemoryPeak (n=14, p95 4.4 GB, max 4.8 GB) - i.e. sized for the worst case, which the comment said was correct until per-worker caps existed. Now they do: MemoryHigh=3G throttles one worker, MemoryMax=6G is the hard stop, TimeoutStartSec=45min kills a wedge, and systemd-oomd kills at 80%/60s. The tail is bounded by the cgroup, not by a pessimistic per-worker budget, so a single 4.8 GB outlier throttles rather than taking the box into swap. Mechanical re-measurement: `bin/ram-measure` (also wired into fleet-heartbeat-tier1 section 14, history at ~/.local/state/ram-measurement/ram-measurement.json, rolling 10 runs). A re-derive of this number is `ram-metric-compare` + jq over ~/.local/state/ram-measurement/ram-metric-compare.json, then a PR; the heartbeat only measures, it never edits this file. Per-task-weight cap: NOT applied. task_weight() in seat-lib.sh distinguishes heavy vs light packets, but the 4.8 GB outlier was a single failed worker, not a class of task (n=14: median 1.28, p95 4.4, max 4.8 - the tail is one data point). Live heavy workers measure 0.8 GB. Revisit if the rolling ram-measure history ever shows heavy-class p95 sustained > 3 GB.

xai-oauth._comment_xai_oauth: fleet-ops#1163 (2026-08-27): SuperGrok prepaid weekly sub, revived via stnly/pi-grok (pi-grok@0.10.1) OAuth provider — different from the api.x.ai 'grok' entry above (which has no live credential). Subscription-backed $0 marginal — fits the 'prepaid subs run at max utilization' rule (cap=1 holds the lane, the live weekly meter must move within minutes of any draw, never-double-wire). Pick a $0 marginal prepaid lane over a $1.20/M minimax metered one. The provider must also be present in ~/.pi/agent/models.json (xai-oauth entry with models grok-4.6 + grok-4.5) for enumerate_seats to emit it; the cap map here is the allowlist, models.json is the inventory. If the OAuth token dies the seat-health extension writes a credentials_bad ledger entry and pick_seat skips the seat — no silent 'ready' lie. The pi-grok extension also self-heals the token (auto-refresh on 401), so a transient 403 should be rare; a persistent one is the dead-credential case this row is wired to catch.
